scope: The 1834 box, whole: the forks, the main stem to the fort, the river turned south behind the baymouth spit to its natural outlet at Swearingen's half mile, the lake shore south of the outlet, and the ground south to the box floor at N -3800 - which takes in the Fort-to-Eighteenth-Street corridor the 1812 scene needs. South of Twelfth Street every vertex is conjectural, by the carried evidence_limit; the battle ground is therefore modelled ground and is NOT a reconstruction from evidence, and this spec says so rather than letting the box's extent imply otherwise.
standard: No survey of this ground exists before Wright's of 1834, and no level of it before the 1850s. Every land elevation here is an 1835 dossier zone carried back twenty-three years, every planform line is a reading of 1834 with the works removed, and the lake stage of 1812 is not recorded at all. So nothing in this spec is better than `inferred`, every surface it AUTHORS for 1812 is `reconstructed`, and the generator must emit no land vertex `documented`.

context.label: Measured relief
context.text: Land in the modelled box runs -3.556 to 13.884 ft above the water surface, and the channel floor reaches -17.409 ft below it. Measured from the committed heightfield, not asserted.

claims.label: lake_stage_1812
notes: No lake stage of 1812 is recorded, and the dossier grades even the 1835 one conjectural (zone 2, 580 +/- 1.5 ft ASL). The water stands at the 1835 plane so the two epochs' ground can be compared and so every carried bank keeps the freeboard its zone gives it; the historic range of 576-582 ft ASL (dossier section 1.2) is the bound, Z -4 to +2. A lower 1812 lake would widen every beach and lower the river against its banks; a higher one would drown the spit, whose chosen crest is +4. Replaced by any stage reconstruction for the 1810s (NOAA/GLERL Michigan-Huron series).

The 1812 water is the plane Z = 0, which generators/terrain_gen_e1830.py writes through terrain_gen.write_heightfield at a literal zero (heightfield.json water_surface_m) rather than reading surface_ft. range_ft is the zone's bound and dossier_zone a record label for the panel; neither is a build input.

transcribes.work: Journal of Lieutenant James Strode Swearingen, kept on the march from Detroit to Chicago in temporary command of the company sent to establish the first Fort Dearborn; entry for Wednesday 17 August 1803, the day of arrival
transcribes.note: Carries the only period measurement of the Chicago river this project has: about 30 yards wide and upwards of 18 feet deep at the fort site, a south bank about 8 feet high half a mile above the mouth, the opposite bank lower by not more than two feet BY APPEARANCES, and the banks above quite low. The last of those is the only sentence in it that reaches the modelled quadrant, and it is the one the encyclopedia paraphrase dropped. Also the pre-cut hydraulic regime in the witness's own words — 'dead water, owing to its being stopped up at the mouth, by the washing of sand' — which is why it does not license the flat surface of the 1835 scene: see docs/RESEARCH/swearingen_1803.md.

what_it_supplies: channel width and depth at the Fort Dearborn site in August 1803, from a witness standing there
the height of the south (fort) bank at that point, about 8 feet
that the north bank was lower, by an estimate made by eye and stated as a maximum of two feet
that the river above the fort had quite low banks — the only statement here about the reach this project models
that the pre-cut river was dead water, and the witness's reason for it: the mouth was stopped up by sand washing in from the lake
the distance from the fort site down to the natural mouth in 1803: half a mile
what_it_does_not_supply: any surface gradient, and therefore no evidence for or against a level water surface as a measurement
any measurement at the forks — every figure here is taken 1.2 miles downstream at the fort site
any measurement after 1803, and the 1833-34 harbour cut removed the condition the witness gives for the river standing dead
a bank height for the modelled quadrant: 'quite low' is qualitative and cannot promote a confidence
the north bank's height as a number — the 6 ft widely quoted from this passage is arithmetic performed on a hedged estimate by later writers, not a figure Swearingen wrote
any planform: the journal draws nothing and no geometry is traced from it

notes: The channel behind the spit, from the fort south to the outlet. The 1834 spec's old_south_channel takes zone 26's middle, -2.5 ft, for a backwater silting into a lagoon after the cut took the river; in 1812 the whole river ran down it, so the DEEP end of zone 26's range is taken, -4 ft. It is not carried down to the main stem's -12 to -18 (zone 20): the bar 'admitted only boats' (dossier section 3.2), the schooner Tracy anchored half a mile out in 1803 for that reason, and Harrison's 1830 plat letters the old mouth 'very shallow'. So the channel is graded shallow and the error, if any, is too shallow for a live river - the direction that does not invent a navigable mouth the record says was not there. Same anchor and e-fold as the 1834 reach so the two epochs differ in depth only.

citations.carries_no_document: Opened and read in full 2026-08-11 (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chicago_River&action=raw, HTTP 200). Looked for a transcription of Swearingen's 1803 journal and there is none: the page paraphrases him in one sentence of its own prose and footnotes the reprinting, which is a citation and not a reprinting. Every other passage this project draws on here is the same shape. So this record's rung is a judgement about an encyclopedia article — later scholarship, tier 4 — and the documents behind it have to be fetched on their own terms. Where it sends you: Quaife 1913, pp. 373-377 for Swearingen; Holland, Chicago in Maps (2005), pp. 102-109 and Andreas vol. 1, pp. 234-235 for the harbour works.

notes: The 1834 bar's surface carried onto the 1812 spit, at the same +4 ft crest and 12 m face (1:9.8, zone 4's beach slope). Of the five reasons the 1834 spec gives for taking zone 7's LOW end, four hold for 1812 and one does not. Holding: the soldiers of Fort Dearborn trenched this bar with hand tools between 1816 and 1828, so it was low enough to dig through in the years after this scene; the 1839 Fort Dearborn Addition reading of the ground east of Michigan Avenue as 'at best ... a low sandbar'; the direction of the error, because an 8 ft ridge here would hide the river behind a dune it never was; and the dossier's own zone 3 ridge at +9 to +10, which the young end of the same littoral system cannot equal. Not holding: the mid-1830s high-water phase, which is an 1835 fact. The 1812 stage is unknown (lake_stage_1812), so it neither raises nor lowers the choice, and +4 stands on the other four. The planform is Wright's 1834 bar carried whole; over most of its length it is 108-164 m wide, wider than zone 7's 100-300 ft, and that is the trace's reading and is not narrowed here. The surface is emitted CONJECTURAL in the confidence channel: its shape is evidence, its height is not.

feature, crest_ft and face_m are read: generators/terrain_gen_e1830.py lifts the spit and its neck to crest_ft across face_m. range_ft is zone 7's bound and dossier_zone a label. material is not drawn: the ground is one surface colour across the box, as the 1834 surface_materials rows declare, and L362 admits it.

notes: L240 left this as a stated hole: the attachment inferred, no ground asserted across it. It gets a SURFACE here, because an 1812 scene with a gap in the spit has the river running out through the place the cut was later dug - the 1834 mouth drawn into 1812, which is the error shore_1812_pre_cut exists to prevent - and because the ground is continuous by the same deduction that made the attachment inferred. What it is: a ribbon of sand 100 ft wide centred on the gap line, its south-west face the river's turn south and its north-east face the lake, at the spit's own +4 ft crest with the spit's own 12 m faces. Width: zone 7's LOW end. The ends of the line are fixed, so a wider neck has to go somewhere, and neither face has a reading; the narrowest neck zone 7 allows is the least land invented, and a neck soldiers cut through again and again with spades is not a broad one. The bar's own width a little south of it (108 m at N +205, the trace) is the upper alternative and is recorded, not adopted. Height: the spit's, because a neck LOWER than the spit is a breach - which is the 1834 storm's landform, not 1812's - and one higher is the zone 3 ridge, which it is not. A pre-1833 chart or sounding of the mouth replaces all of it. docs/LIBERTIES.md records it.

decision, feature, width_ft, crest_ft and face_m are read: generators/terrain_gen_e1830.py lays the ribbon width_ft wide on the feature's own line. centreline restates that line in words and is not parsed; the zone fields are labels and bounds.

notes: THE 1812 SHORE NORTH OF THE SPIT ROOT IS NOT READ ANYWHERE, AND A WATERLINE HAS TO BE SOMEWHERE. derive_shore_1812.py deliberately claims none of it: from index 30 to the pier head the 1834 line is the drafted pier, and from index 39 north it is a shore the 1834 epoch says is accreting against the pier (zone 28, a wedge 100-300 ft wide tapering north). Sand caught updrift of a pier was not there before the pier, so the 1812 shore lay WEST of the 1834 one near the root; that sets the direction, and nothing sets the amount. So the line is the least-land one the two committed points allow: a straight chord from the spit root to the first 1834 vertex past the pier head, then the 1834 line north. The chord cuts off the drafted pier and the sand inside it, up to 120.8 m (396 ft) east of the chord at index 34. That is more than zone 28's 300 ft because the drafted pier head and the pier's own width stand inside the triangle beside the sand it caught, and both are absent in 1812. North of index 39 the 1834 line is carried AS the 1812 shore, which overstates the land by whatever the wedge still held there. Both errors run one way, toward too much beach north of the root and never toward an invented headland. docs/LIBERTIES.md records it; a pre-1833 chart of the lake shore replaces it.

The run is built by generators/terrain_gen_e1830.py from the two committed points the run block names (1834 index 29 and the mouth readings' accretion_bound_first_index); dossier_zone is a record label.
